common_affordance: The selected links may connect priority locations through arbitrarily many intermediate locations, making the problem the standard weighted Steiner-tree problem.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It reduces the problem to an MST on pairwise shortest-path distances between priority locations, which can double-count shared intermediate infrastructure and misses cheaper Steiner trees.
It likewise applies an MST-style reduction over terminal distances instead of optimizing a shared subgraph containing non-priority Steiner vertices.

recommended_edit: Replace “possibly passing through multiple intermediate locations” with “passing through at most one intermediate location on any route between two priority locations,” and similarly limit the preceding permission to use at most one other location.
regression_risk: This could restore the already-defeated MST-based solutions on instances where the one-intermediate restriction makes the optimum equivalent to an MST over terminal-to-terminal options.
